subject: MAP: evaluation playbook, reproduction plan, and competitive audit

Subject: MAP: benchmarking plan + method alignment request

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Acme is excited about the latency and cost claims. Before we lock the MAP, we need a concrete evaluation plan we can drop into procurement and engineering. Specifically we want:

- A repeatable benchmarking plan covering latency (p50/p95), TTFT, throughput and concurrency.
- Clear methodology notes so our SREs can reproduce results in our cloud account.
- A timeline: we have an internal procurement milestone 12/10 and would like MAP signoff + final pricing before that.

Two additional asks:
1) We plan to compare to OrchidAI in our internal benchmark — any guidance on avoiding toolchain mismatches would help.
2) Is there a minimal dataset and command set we can run (not your raw infra) to validate parity?

Can you share a draft MAP section (bench plan + expected results) and an engineer-facing repro guide by EOD Monday?

Jordan

Jordan — thanks, appreciate the clarity. Attached is a draft MAP section (ACME_MAP_Benchmark_v1.xlsx) and a short repro guide (repro_guide_v1.md) that our SRE/bench team uses for customer parity checks. Quick summary below and proposed timeline: 

Summary of proposed eval plan (TL;DR)
- Scope: 3 workloads (small chat, long-context summarization, and embedding bulk inference).
- Metrics: TTFT (95th), token latency p50/p95, sustained throughput (tokens/sec), and end-to-end tail concurrency behavior.
- Environment: we ask to run in us-west-2 (or specify your preferred region) with a dedicated test project + one VM for load driver.
- Model pin: redwood-rw-v2-13b (server-side pinned; we provide compatible 8-bit quantized image for Dedicated/private tests).

Customer repro guidance (high level)
- We include a small harness (redwood-bench) with example flags in repro_guide_v1.md. Run with --seq-len 2048 and --warmup 200 to stabilize kernels.
- TTFT definition: time from request accept to first token emitted; report p50/p95 over 1k requests per workload.
- Concurrency: run 1, 4, 8, 16 simultaneous clients to profile scaling floor.

Proposed timeline (compact to meet your procurement target)
- Mon/Tue (11/30–12/01): alignment call to finalize repro environment and Hub project + share short-lived test creds.
- Wed–Fri (12/02–12/04): Acme runs baseline on OrchidAI and our provided harness.
- Mon–Tue (12/07–12/08): we run mirrored tests on our infra and exchange CSVs for parity analysis.
- 12/09: joint readout and MAP finalization; aim for 12/10 procurement submission.

Note on competitive comparisons
- Toolchain mismatches (PyTorch vs. TF, different tokenizer implementations, or server-level batching semantics) are the most common cause of delta. Our guide includes normalization steps (tokenizer seed, exact prompt templates, and disabling server-side auto-batching) to reduce noise.

I'll loop in Karthik (bench lead) for the deeper method notes and a runnable command set. Please confirm the preferred region and whether we should include OrchidAI-flagged test cases in the initial run.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz

Jordan — adding a few concrete, engineer-facing notes so your SREs can reproduce and so we have apples-to-apples comparisons: 

Execution environment guidance
- Use a single-threaded load driver per client process to avoid jitter from multi-threaded drivers. We recommend k6 or our redwood-bench harness (attached commands).
- Pin sequence length at 2048 for long-context runs. For chat, use variable prompt lengths but bucketed so that median and 95th are comparable.

Measurement definitions (please adopt exactly these to avoid ambiguity)
- TTFT: time from TCP accept to first token byte emitted; measure at the client (not sampled on server) and report p50/p95/p99.
- Token latency: token emission intervals measured on client; report per-token p50/p95.
- Throughput: sustained tokens/sec measured over a 60s window after warmup; report mean and stdev.

Commands (example using redwood-bench)
- redwood-bench run --model redwood-rw-v2-13b --host api.redwood.ai --seq-len 2048 --concurrency 8 --requests 1000 --warmup 200 --measure ttft,latency,throughput --out results_acme_redwood.csv
- For OrchidAI baseline: use their recommended client but match tokenizer and prompt templates exactly; export raw tokens for parity checks.

Common pitfalls we see
- Tokenizer mismatches: use the same tokenizer binary or compare tokenized lengths rather than raw text.
- Server auto-batching: if OrchidAI or a comparator batches aggressively, disable or set batch window to 1ms to match our default.
- KV cache differences: when reproducing long-context workloads, ensure left-padding and prompt continuation rules match.

I'll also attach a small validation script (we can provide on the call) that compares token-level latency histograms and flags >10% p95 deltas for manual review.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Bench & Runtime
